header:
Date: 2027-05-14
Time: 15:00 - 15:52 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Torres (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood CSM), Ethan Wu (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Singh (Clearmap Head of Data), Liam O'Connor (Clearmap CTO), Sara Park (Clearmap DevOps)
Recording: yes
Notes: kickoff / onboarding / implementation
summary: Kickoff call to align on Clearmap Health onboarding to Redwood. Covered architecture options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security/compliance needs (SOC2, KMS, VPC peering), initial bench targets, data handling and PII concerns, success criteria and timeline. Agreed next steps: share onboarding checklist, sample payloads, schedule performance benchmark, weekly syncs.
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Jamie from Redwood, im the account exec on this one. quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya: hi yes maya here, glad to be on.
[00:11] Liam: liam here, ct-o, yep.
[00:13] Sara: sara, devops.
[00:16] Priya: priya from customer success at redwood.
[00:18] Ethan: ethan se, i'll drive the technical bits.
[00:21] Jamie: perfect ok so goal for today is to align on scope, security, and the first pilot, and outline the runbook. we'll go through architecture options and then get into benchmarks. sound good?
[00:36] Maya: sounds good. quick context, we have a clinical triage product, want to use embeddings + chat to power notes summarization and triage suggestions, data is PHI so HIPAA sensitivity.
[00:52] Liam: timeline wise we want a pilot in production-ish traffic in about 6 weeks, ideally.
[00:58] Jamie: great, that helps. priya, can you run through the onboarding phases briefly?
[01:05] Priya: yeah sure. phases are: kickoff, infra setup (vpc or dedicated), data integration + test datasets, pilot bench and quality evals, then rollout. i'll send the checklist after this call.
[01:18] Sara: on infra, we need private deployment or dedicated? security team prefers VPC and customer-managed keys.
[01:27] Ethan: ok on the options: we support Hosted API (fastest), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). for PHI and KMS we typically recommend Private or Dedicated with VPC peering and customer KMS. note: dedicated can be isolated but keys are usually through our KMS integration unless you choose Private.
[01:49] Maya: when you say KMS integration, is that bring-your-own-key/hsm?
[01:54] Ethan: yes we integrate with customer KMS, and HSM for private deployments. there was an earlier doc i think titled hsm-integration.pdf — i'll share link. small caveat, onboarding for private is a bit longer, maybe 4-8 weeks depending on network and audit.
[02:09] Liam: that's okay as long as pilot can run in the meantime. could we start with hosted for development and move to private for prod?
[02:16] Jamie: absolutely, many customers do dev on Hosted then switch to Dedicated/Private for prod. tradeoffs: hosted is easiest but has higher per-token cost and you need to validate data residency controls; dedicated gives predictability on latency and throughput; private gives max control and compliance.
[02:34] Ethan: for performance, we usually recommend a benchmark with a 99th percentile latency goal. what's your latency SLO?
[02:41] Maya: sub-200ms 95p for single-turn summarization would be ideal but we can be flexible, depends on batch sizes.
[02:49] Ethan: ok that helps. sample plan: we'll run a perf test with a realistic distribution of sequence lengths and concurrency. we can test quantized variants too. i'll propose kernels and batch sizes.
[03:03] Jamie: can we talk about success criteria? maya?
[03:07] Maya: success is: accurate summarizations (ROUGE-ish metrics we'll provide eval sets), latency under 200ms for 95p, and no PHI leakage in logs; also need audit logs and retention controls.
[03:19] Priya: noted. we'll map these to the onboarding checklist. regarding logs, Redwood supports audit logs and retention configs, we'll share SOC2 whitepaper and audit docs.
[03:30] Liam: on SOC2, our compliance team will want the report and any additional attestation around encryption in transit and at rest.
[03:36] Ethan: we have SOC2 plus ISO certs for the control plane in hosted; for private deployments you can maintain your own control plane and KMS. we'll share the compliance pack.
[03:45] Sara: networking: what firewall rules and VPC peering do you need?
[03:49] Ethan: for VPC peering, typical is allow outbound to redwood management IPs on ports 443, and open specific subnets for inference egress. i'll send a template for AWS/GCP. also note that some customers use NAT + SSM tunnels for private — depends on your security posture.
[04:06] Maya: on data, we will scrub PHI in dev but pilot will have de-identified sets; production needs full PHI support with BAA. do you have a BAA?
[04:16] Jamie: yes we execute BAAs for enterprise private deployments. i'll loop legal.
[04:20] Liam: great. one more: cost. we have concerns about token costs with large volumes. how are you advising?
[04:26] Priya: cost levers: batching, caching (prefix + KV cache), model quantization and choosing model variants. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching profiles per workload. we'll include cost estimates in the follow-up.
[04:39] Maya: does Redwood provide per-route cost breakdowns for auditing?
[04:44] Ethan: yes redwood console has per-route and per-token breakdowns, you can tag routes and see cost per tag. small note: console naming got mis-typed sometimes in our docs as 'Redwood Console' vs 'Redwood Consolee' in a few older PDFs — ignore that.
[04:58] Jamie: haha noted.
[05:00] [05:00] Speaker 1: (noise)
[05:08] Ethan: back to benchmarks, do you have expected QPS?
[05:12] Liam: during pilot maybe 5-10 QPS peak, production could be 50-100 depending on adoption.
[05:19] Ethan: ok we'll size the dedicated pool around that and propose autoscaling/burst config. also we'll run a spot check to see model memory with your average sequence length.
[05:32] Maya: we also want to run quality regression checks between model versions and have alerts if summarization drifts.
[05:38] Priya: we have an evals workflow; you can upload a prompt set and we run regression alerts. we'll tie that to the monitoring dashboard.
[05:45] Sara: who will own rollout? devops or product?
[05:48] Liam: devops will do infra but product owns quality. devops will handle network/infra setup.
[05:53] Jamie: ok responsibilities noted.
[05:56] [06:00] Jamie: quick Q on integrations — do you need SDKs, or will you call the REST API?
[06:05] Maya: we'll probably use REST from backend services, maybe go SDKs later.
[06:10] Ethan: we support REST, python and go SDKs; we'll share code samples for streaming and structured output.
[06:18] Maya: streaming is key for UX.
[06:21] Ethan: yes streaming and function-calls, we support structured outputs that make post-processing easier.
[06:28] Liam: security again — SAML SSO for your console?
[06:32] Priya: yes we support SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning; for private you can use your identity provider.
[06:38] Sara: any gotchas for our infra team?
[06:40] Ethan: watch out for MTU and TLS inspection appliances; they sometimes break streaming connections. also kvcache warmup if you do prefix caching we can provide strategies to pre-warm.
[06:55] Maya: about model versions — we want the ability to pin to a version and roll back if quality drops.
[07:00] Ethan: supported, we do canary and A/B rollouts and automatic fallback to a compatible variant; we'll include rollout docs.
[07:09] Jamie: ok next chunk is timeline and immediate asks.
[07:13] Priya: immediate asks: 1) clearmap to share sample payloads and traffic profile 2) redwood to share onboarding checklist, compliance pack, and network templates 3) schedule perf benchmark with ethan. i'll send calendar invites.
[07:27] Liam: we can get sample payloads by next thursday.
[07:30] Sara: security will confirm firewall rules by tuesday.
[07:34] Maya: also want to run a short quality baseline with current model outputs — we'll share some labeled examples.
[07:40] Ethan: perfect, include sequence length distrib and token histograms if you can.
[07:45] [15:00] Jamie: jumping ahead a bit, pricing for dedicated vs hosted — we usually provide an estimate based on traffic profile; dedicated is commit-based. i'll follow up with a pricing spreadsheet.
[15:12] Liam: ok. also procurement wants an initial MSA and BAA draft to review in parallel.
[15:19] Jamie: i'll loop legal and share MSA + BAA templates.
[15:24] Maya: any blockers you see?
[15:28] Ethan: nothing big beyond network/keys and sample data. private will take longer but pilot path is clear.
[15:34] Priya: we'll set up weekly 30-minute calls; first one 2027-05-21 15:00 UTC unless that's problematic.
[15:42] Liam: works for us.
[15:45] Sara: works.
[15:48] Jamie: ok recap: priya will send onboarding checklist + weekly invites; ethan will share benchmark plan; liam/sara/maya will provide payloads and security answers. legal will get MSA/BAA. agreed?
[16:04] Maya: agreed.
[16:06] Jamie: thanks everyone, i'll send a one-pager and a link to the onboarding docs — Link: https://redwood.example.com/onboarding/clearmap-checklist
[16:15] [16:15] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
[16:20] Jamie: end of notes — thanks all, talk soon.
